individuals.title: Bottle filling: one measurement per hour
individuals.description: Synthetic teaching data. Sixty bottle volumes recorded in collection order; a deliberate mean shift begins at observation 41.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
One different bottle is sampled at each time point.
Keep sequence order for an individuals and moving-range chart.
The simulated shift is a teaching feature, not a statistical conclusion computed by the guide.

subgroups.title: Shaft diameter: 5 parts per subgroup
subgroups.description: Synthetic teaching data. Twenty-five ordered subgroups, each containing 5 different shafts produced close together in time.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
These are distinct parts within each subgroup, not repeated readings of one part.
Choose long-format input with diameter_mm as the measurement and subgroup as the subgroup identifier.
A mean shift is introduced in subgroups 21–25.

subgroups_large.title: Shaft diameter: 10 parts per subgroup
subgroups_large.description: Synthetic teaching data. Twenty-five ordered subgroups, each containing 10 different shafts produced close together in time.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
These are distinct parts within each subgroup, not repeated readings of one part.
Choose long-format input with diameter_mm as the measurement and subgroup as the subgroup identifier.
The generator uses a constant mean and standard deviation; random samples can nevertheless produce chart signals.

passfail.title: Rejected units: 100 units per batch
passfail.description: Synthetic teaching data. Each item is classified once as conforming or nonconforming. The rejection probability increases after batch 20.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
rejected is a count of nonconforming units, not a count of individual defects.
Use inspected as the denominator; do not enter percentages as rejected.
The sample size is 100 throughout, permitting either a p chart or an np chart.

passfail_varying.title: Rejected units: varying sample sizes
passfail_varying.description: Synthetic teaching data. Each item is classified once as conforming or nonconforming. The rejection probability increases after batch 20.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
rejected is a count of nonconforming units, not a count of individual defects.
Use inspected as the denominator; do not enter percentages as rejected.
A p chart accommodates these varying denominators.

defects.title: Surface defects: 10 panels per batch
defects.description: Synthetic teaching data. Defects are counted on comparable panels. One panel can have several defects; the defect intensity rises after batch 20.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
The number of defects can exceed the number of panels inspected.
Each panel represents the same area and opportunity for defects.
Each batch contains 10 panels, giving a constant opportunity for a c chart; a u chart is also possible.

defects_varying.title: Surface defects: varying inspected quantities
defects_varying.description: Synthetic teaching data. Defects are counted on comparable panels. One panel can have several defects; the defect intensity rises after batch 20.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
The number of defects can exceed the number of panels inspected.
Each panel represents the same area and opportunity for defects.
Use a u chart with units_inspected as exposure.

cap_spread.title: Bottle fill: too much variation
cap_spread.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred and twenty independently generated bottle volumes in collection order.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Illustrative requirements: lower specification 490 mL, upper specification 510 mL, target 500 mL.
The generator is centered on the target, but its spread is large relative to the specification interval.
The data-generating mean and standard deviation are constant. Examine the realized time plot before interpreting capability.
Compare this example with the other bottle-fill capability dataset; do not pool them.

cap_offcenter.title: Bottle fill: a shifted process center
cap_offcenter.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred and twenty independently generated bottle volumes in collection order.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Illustrative requirements: lower specification 490 mL, upper specification 510 mL, target 500 mL.
The generator has modest spread, but its mean is close to the upper specification limit.
The data-generating mean and standard deviation are constant. Examine the realized time plot before interpreting capability.
Compare this example with the other bottle-fill capability dataset; do not pool them.

cap_skew.title: Cycle time: a right-skewed distribution
cap_skew.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred and fifty positive cycle times sampled from a lognormal distribution with median 25 seconds.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Illustrative requirement: upper specification 60 seconds; there is no lower specification.
The generator is lognormal with log-scale standard deviation 0.48. This is known only because the example is simulated.
In real data, use process knowledge and fit diagnostics, especially the relevant tail, before choosing a capability distribution.
Zero is a physical boundary, not an automatically imposed lower specification.

gage.title: Crossed Gauge R&R: shaft diameters
gage.description: Synthetic teaching data. Ten parts are each measured by three operators on two occasions, giving 60 readings.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
All operators measure the same physical parts: this is a crossed design.
part and operator are categorical identifiers; diameter_mm is a scale variable.
The simulated measurement variation contains operator, operator-by-part, and repeatability components.
In a real study, randomize measurement order and conceal previous readings where feasible.

gage_nested.title: Nested Gauge R&R: destructive strength readings
gage_nested.description: Synthetic teaching data. Each operator receives 10 distinct homogeneous specimen batches and tests two nominally equivalent specimens from each batch.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
part identifies a specimen batch unique to one operator; batches are nested within operators.
replicate identifies separate specimens, because the strength test destroys each specimen.
Within-batch specimen equivalence is an assumption of this example. If it is false, specimen variation and measurement variation are confounded.
Destructive testing alone does not determine nesting; the allocation of batches to operators does.

gage_type1.title: Type 1 study: one length reference
gage_type1.description: Synthetic teaching data. One operator makes 50 repeated readings of a reference whose accepted value is 25.000 mm.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Reference value: 25.000 mm. Illustrative total tolerance width: 0.100 mm.
The generator includes a positive bias of 0.004 mm and repeatability standard deviation of 0.002 mm.
This study addresses one instrument/operator/reference setting; it does not estimate between-operator reproducibility.

linearity.title: Gauge linearity: five reference lengths
linearity.description: Synthetic teaching data. Ten repeated readings are obtained at each of five accepted reference lengths across the operating range.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
The simulated bias changes linearly with reference value and is zero at 30 mm.
reference_mm contains accepted reference values, not estimates from these repeated readings.
Assess bias across the working range and inspect residual variation; do not extrapolate calibration beyond that range.

agreement.title: Attribute agreement: visual inspection
agreement.description: Synthetic teaching data. Three inspectors classify the same 12 parts twice as Pass or Fail. A trusted reference classification is supplied.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
part, operator, rating, and standard are categorical; trial labels the inspection occasion.
Within-inspector consistency, between-inspector agreement, and agreement with standard answer different questions.
The example is deliberately imperfect. Inspect the pattern of errors as well as any single agreement coefficient.

compare_single.title: Fill weight versus a 500 g target
compare_single.description: Synthetic teaching data. Sixty independent package weights for a one-sample mean comparison.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Test/reference value: 500 g.
An illustrative equivalence question uses acceptable mean differences of −1 to +1 g, defined before looking at the results.
The equivalence margin concerns the population mean, not acceptance limits for individual packages.

compare_ind.title: Two suppliers: independent shaft diameters
compare_ind.description: Synthetic teaching data. Thirty different shafts from each of two suppliers, with deliberately unequal population spreads.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
No shaft occurs in both groups: these are independent samples.
Measurement is in millimeters; Group and Part are categorical.
For an illustrative equivalence question, use acceptable mean differences of −0.05 to +0.05 mm only if justified independently of these data.
Equivalence of means does not demonstrate equal variability or equal defect rates.

compare_paired.title: Before and after: paired task completion times
compare_paired.description: Synthetic teaching data. The same 30 test tasks are performed under the original and revised workflow.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Each row is one matched pair; preserve the row correspondence.
Analyze within-pair differences and inspect their distribution.
Illustrative equivalence margins for a mean time difference are −1 to +1 second.
A real before/after study may confound the workflow change with learning, order, or time trends.

compare_three.title: Three machines: independent shaft diameters
compare_three.description: Synthetic teaching data. Twenty-five different shafts are sampled from each of three machines.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Group identifies the machine; each Part occurs only once.
An omnibus comparison concerns whether all group means are equal; planned contrasts or multiplicity-adjusted comparisons answer more specific questions.
The same nominal standard deviation is used in each generating population, but sample standard deviations will differ.

repeated_three.title: Three settings: repeated readings on the same parts
repeated_three.description: Synthetic teaching data. Twenty-four stable calibration parts are each measured under three instrument settings.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Each row represents the same part in all three columns; this is a repeated-measures design.
Create one within-subject factor with three levels and assign Setting_A, Setting_B, and Setting_C to those levels.
This comparison of mean settings is not a complete Gauge R&R study.
In a real study, counterbalance or randomize setting order to reduce order effects.

passfail_units.title: One batch: individual pass/fail results
passfail_units.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred and twenty independent items each receive a single inspection outcome.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Result is a two-level nominal variable.
When testing a nonconformance proportion, explicitly choose Fail as the event of interest.
An illustrative benchmark is a failure probability of 0.05; justify the benchmark and test direction before inspecting the outcome.

contingency.title: Suppliers and inspection outcome: aggregated counts
contingency.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred independent items are inspected from each supplier; the worksheet stores six aggregated frequency cells.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Supplier and Result define the table; place Count in the frequency/counts field.
These six rows summarize 300 items. Do not analyze the six rows as if they were six individual inspections.
Inspect expected cell counts and use an appropriate exact method if needed.

factorial.title: Replicated two-level factorial: bond strength
factorial.description: Synthetic teaching data. A complete 2³ factorial is independently replicated twice and randomized, giving 16 experimental runs.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Natural low/high settings: Temperature 160/180 °C; Pressure 2/4 bar; Speed 40/60 rpm.
Coded values −1/+1 correspond to these low/high settings; centers are 170 °C, 3 bar, and 50 rpm.
Rows with repeated settings are separate experimental runs, not repeated readings from the same run.
The generating model contains main effects plus Temperature × Pressure and Pressure × Speed interactions.
The randomized Run column records execution order. No center points or blocks are included.

surface.title: Response surface: temperature, time, and yield
surface.description: Synthetic teaching data. A two-factor face-centered central composite design has four factorial points, four axial points, and five independently replicated center runs.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Temperature settings: 160, 170, 180 °C. Time settings: 20, 30, 40 minutes.
Coding: (Temperature − 170)/10 and (Time − 30)/10. Axial distance is 1 (face-centered).
There are 13 randomized experimental runs; Yield is a continuous percentage, not a binomial count.
The generating model includes both linear terms, both squared terms, and their interaction.
Fit a second-order model, inspect residuals, and confirm any proposed optimum in new runs.

drivers.title: Process drivers: continuous yield
drivers.description: Synthetic teaching data. Seventy-two production observations contain temperature, pressure, and a continuous yield measurement.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Temperature spans 155–185 °C; Pressure spans 1.5–4.5 bar.
Yield is a continuous percentage; no inspected-item denominator is available or implied.
Use Temperature and Pressure as predictors and Yield as the response; Run is an identifier.
This example illustrates association. Observational regression alone does not identify causal effects.
Inspect residual patterns and influential observations; evaluate prediction on independent data.

binary_drivers.title: Process drivers: probability of a defective item
binary_drivers.description: Synthetic teaching data. One hundred and eighty independently generated items have two process measurements and a binary inspection outcome.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
Defective is coded 0 = conforming and 1 = defective. Set it to nominal and verify which level is modeled as the event.
Temperature and Pressure are continuous predictors; Item is an identifier.
A logistic model relates the predictors to event probability while keeping predictions between zero and one.
A rare outcome and limited data can lead to imprecise estimates; inspect uncertainty and predictive performance.

defects_half_panel_preview.title: Flaws per half-panel area — preview
defects_half_panel_preview.description: Synthetic teaching data: all original varying-exposure observations and counts, with an equivalent half-panel area denominator.
notes: Simulated with a fixed random seed; not real production data.
The number of defects can exceed the number of panels inspected.
Each panel represents the same area and opportunity for defects.
Use a u chart with units_inspected as exposure.

Ordinary u preview: exposure_half_panel_units = 2 × units_inspected. One exposure unit is half a panel’s area, not an additional inspected panel. All 30 counts remain; rates and limits halve. Center .383333 defects per half-panel area. The current axis may say Proportion and the rule table misses batch 27. Compare each point with its own limits: batch 27 has .7 against UCL .677017 and is the sole beyond-limit point.
Original defects_varying data are preserved separately.

agreement_ab_preview.title: A/B attribute agreement — two-appraiser preview
agreement_ab_preview.description: Synthetic two-appraiser demonstration: retain the original 48 A/B ratings of 12 parts across two trials; C is outside this preview.
notes: Explicit two-appraiser A/B demonstration: 48 original ratings, all 12 parts and both trials; Positive reference = Pass. Appraiser C is excluded because perfect agreement triggers a confidence-interval failure. The full original 72-rating dataset remains separately available in the example library. For each appraiser, 10/12 parts agree across trials, 22/24 ratings agree with the standard, kappa .828571; missed failures 1/10 and false alarms 1/14.

compare_single_deviation_preview.title: Fill deviation from 500 g — equivalence preview
compare_single_deviation_preview.description: Synthetic teaching data: preserve all 60 original FillWeight values and add their deviation from 500 g.
notes: Preserve all 60 measurements and derive FillWeight_deviation_g = FillWeight − 500. Test against 0 with raw bounds −1/+1 g, alpha .05. This avoids the ignored nonzero-reference problem. Mean deviation .3776667 g, 90% CI [−.0679096,.8232429]. Both tests reject: lower-bound hypothesis t=5.166813, p=.000001480; upper-bound hypothesis t=−2.334004, p=.0115105. The current lower/upper test-row labels are interchanged; interpret the hypotheses and interval, not those row labels.

factorial_preview_eight.title: Eight-run factorial worksheet — unreplicated preview
factorial_preview_eight.description: Synthetic teaching design generated natively in JASP with seed 261107; eight randomized runs and no collected responses.
notes: Create one unreplicated full 2³ design: eight randomized runs, Temperature 160/180 °C, Pressure 2/4 bar, Speed 40/60 rpm, one block (no blocking restriction), no center points, seed 261107. This avoids unwanted replicate blocks. All eight combinations occur once. Response is blank until data collection; replication-based error estimation is unavailable. The original completed 16-run example is preserved separately for Analyse Design.
